title: Physical Activity Interventions For Depressive Symptoms In Older Adults: A Systematic Review (DEMO, Synthetic Data)
contact: demo author, via the repository issue tracker
rationale: Depressive symptoms are common in later life; physical activity is a low-cost option whose effect across intervention types is unclear.
question: In adults aged 60 or older, do structured physical activity interventions reduce depressive symptoms compared with usual care or attention control?
population: Adults aged 60 or older, community-dwelling or in residential care
intervention: Structured physical activity (aerobic, resistance, mind-body, or digitally coached exercise)
comparator: Usual care, waitlist, or attention control
outcomes: Primary: depressive symptoms on a validated scale (GDS, PHQ-9). Secondary: adherence, adverse events
grey_literature: Reference lists of included studies; trial registers
search_string: ("older adult*" OR elderly OR "aged 60") AND (exercise OR "physical activity" OR walking OR "tai chi" OR yoga) AND (depress* OR "low mood")
screening_reviewers: Two independent reviewers at title/abstract and full text; pilot on 10% of records
extraction_items: Design, country, sample size, intervention, comparator, outcome measure; two extractors, piloted form
missing_data: Contact corresponding authors once; otherwise report as missing
synthesis_plan: Structured narrative synthesis by intervention type; meta-analysis only if at least 3 trials share an outcome measure
timeline: Search month 1, screening months 2-3, synthesis month 4
